newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's upgrades 11 Philippine bank ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrades 11 Philippine bank ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had upgraded the long-term foreign currency debt and deposit ratings of 11 Philippine banks.
Moody's also affirmed the short-term ratings of the banks at "not prime" and affirmed their individual Bank Financial Strength Ratings.
The banks' new ratings are as follows:
Bank Senior long-term Long-term
debt deposits
Allied Bank Ba1 Ba2
Bank of the Philippine Is -- Ba2
Development Bank of the Philippines Ba1 Ba2
Equitable Bank -- Ba2
Far East Bank and Trust Ba1 Ba2
Land Bank of the Philippines -- Ba2
Metropolitan Bank and Trust Ba1 Ba2
Philippine Commercial Int'l Ba1 Ba2
Philippine National Bank Ba1 Ba2
Rizal Commercial Bank -- Ba2
United Coconut Planters Bank Ba1 Ba2
Moody's said the banks have strong capital protection, good asset quality, profitability and a vigilant regulatory environment.
However, the rating agency said, assets have grown rapidly over the past three years, especially in consumer financing, and competition from foreign banks will increase the pressure on margins.
"Concerns have been raised about the bank's exposure to the real estate sector, although current exposures appear to be reasonable," Moody's said in a release.
Moody's said the banks' foreign currency ratings are constrained by the Ba1 sovereign ceiling of the Philippines.
It said the rating differential between the country's bond and deposit obligations reflects the greater vulnerability to rescheduling of deposits relative to bonds in a stress scenario.
